answer: Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 5 bits per word is rejected before grading, because it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. Because the entropy is measured at the hollow gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the atlas audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. A farm emitting 193 variations of one paragraph therefore burns for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the terrace panel. That is 14 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
